mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to turn negative due to tightened credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > (current value + 0.25%) in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior month's mean (t-test p > 0.05) during the identified rising rate period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment months) of at least 2,000 above the prior month's level is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return, reflecting consumer confidence and risk-on sentiment.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 60-day forward returns do not exceed the average of the 12 months before the trigger by more than one standard deviation.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly HOUST (residential building permits) exceeds 1.5% above its prior month's level, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, indicating stronger housing demand and economic momentum.
failure_condition: Across 10 such triggers, the average 20-day return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 3% predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to weakening supply-side activity and reduced market expansionary potential.
failure_condition: Over 5 consecutive months of INDPRO declines, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative in at least 80% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE (unemployment rate) by at least 0.2% each, over a 3-month window, drive a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as investors anticipate a normalization in policy tightening.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < (prev month) 0.2% AND UNRATE < (prev month) 0.2% for 3 consecutive months
regime_hint: Dual softening in policy and labor markets
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 12-month pre-trigger average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly UNRATE drop below 3.5% triggers a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as lower unemployment is interpreted as a pro-business labor environment.
failure_condition: Over 10 such triggers, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly GDPC1 (GDP chain) exceeds 2% above its prior month's value in a non-recessionary regime, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive, reflecting robust economic demand.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > (previous month GDPC1) * 1.02 AND regime_hint: not in 'recessionary' regime
failure_condition: During 10 such events, the 20-day forward returns are not higher than the prior month's average by more than one standard deviation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in RSAFS (commercial and industrial loan growth) of 4% or more predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals credit contraction and reduced business investment.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < (previous month RSAFS) * 0.96 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: During 5 such contractions, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).
